prompt: Find the Cartesian equation of the plane through $A(1,0,2)$, $B(2,1,0)$ and $C(0,3,1)$.

concept: Parametric vector equation of a plane
prompt: Using $A(1,0,2)$, $B(2,1,0)$ and $C(0,3,1)$, write down a vector equation of the plane $ABC$ in the form $\mathbf r=\mathbf a+\lambda\mathbf b+\mu\mathbf c$, and explain why $\mathbf b$ and $\mathbf c$ must not be parallel.
markscheme:
$\mathbf r=\begin{pmatrix}1\\0\\2\end{pmatrix}+\lambda\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\\-2\end{pmatrix}+\mu\begin{pmatrix}-1\\3\\-1\end{pmatrix}$ **(A1)**

Two parallel directions only describe a line; two non-parallel directions are needed to span a plane **(R1)**

prompt: Write the plane through $(2,-1,3)$ with normal $\mathbf n=\begin{pmatrix}1\\4\\-2\end{pmatrix}$ in the forms $\mathbf r\cdot\mathbf n=\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf n$ and $ax+by+cz=d$.
markscheme:
$\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf n=2-4-6=-8$ **(A1)**: $\mathbf r\cdot\begin{pmatrix}1\\4\\-2\end{pmatrix}=-8$, i.e. $x+4y-2z=-8$ **(A1)**

Every point $\mathbf r$ on the plane has $\mathbf r-\mathbf a$ perpendicular to $\mathbf n$, which is what $(\mathbf r-\mathbf a)\cdot\mathbf n=0$ says.

prompt: Explain why the equation $\mathbf r=\mathbf a+\lambda\mathbf b$ cannot describe a plane, but $\mathbf r\cdot\mathbf n=\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf n$ can.
markscheme: $\mathbf r=\mathbf a+\lambda\mathbf b$ has one parameter, so it gives points along one direction only — a line. $\mathbf r\cdot\mathbf n=\mathbf a\cdot\mathbf n$ is satisfied by every point whose displacement from $A$ is perpendicular to $\mathbf n$, which fills a whole plane **(R1)**
